commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG user stories for TutorTrack
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide still lists AB3's address-book user stories,
which describe managing generic contacts rather than a private
tutor's student roster.

Replace them with TutorTrack's user stories so the guide records
the full requirements of the product:

* must-have stories for the MVP loop of adding, listing, viewing,
  noting, and deleting students
* nice-to-have stories for edit, find, undo, and help
* unlikely stories for sample data, archiving, restoring, and
  sibling linking, kept to show what was considered but excluded

Remove the "More to be added" placeholder, as the list now covers
all identified requirements.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG user stories for TutorTrack
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide lists AB3's address-book user stories, which
describe managing generic contacts rather than a private tutor's
student roster.

The DG must cover the full requirements of TutorTrack, including
stories considered but not planned, so readers can see the scope
of the product and the priority of each feature.

Replace the AB3 stories with TutorTrack's user stories:

* must-have stories for adding, listing, viewing, noting, and
  deleting students, plus duplicate checks and saving
* nice-to-have stories for editing, finding, undo, help, and
  sample data
* unlikely stories for archiving, sibling linking, note editing,
  and multi-computer access, kept to show what was considered

Use one term for each concept, such as roster, student, parent
contact, and session note, so that no two stories describe the
same thing in different words.

Two user stories in the Developer Guide have weak wording. One
uses the British spelling "misspelt", while the rest of the guide
uses American spelling. Another has a benefit, "see all my
students again", that only restates its want of returning to the
full roster.

A benefit that repeats its want, and inconsistent spelling, are
flagged as user story and documentation bugs during grading.

Use the American spelling "misspelled", and give the return-to-
roster story a distinct benefit: selecting any student by their
roster number again.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark Beryl scripts and git hooks as executable
commitResults.messageBody:
Every Beryl script and git hook is stored without the executable
bit, so documented commands such as ./.beryl/scripts/check.sh fail
with "Permission denied", and agent-doctor.sh rejects the install.

Set the executable bit on all Beryl scripts and hooks, so the check
gate and doctor run as documented on every clone.

Markdown Formatting Fix For NFRs

TutorTrack has no way to represent what happened in a lesson, so
tutors cannot record session notes yet.

Let's add an immutable SessionNote holding the note text and the
OffsetDateTime at which it was recorded. The text is stripped of
surrounding whitespace and must be 1 to 500 printable characters on
one line, with internal spaces kept as typed.

Length is counted in code points so that an emoji counts as one
character. The caller supplies the timestamp, which keeps the type
deterministic to test and leaves timestamping to the model.

Each student needs an ordered record of their session notes, with
the most recent note easy to find.

Let's add an immutable SessionHistory that keeps notes newest first.
withNote(...) returns a new history and leaves the original
unchanged, so the model can prepare a change before saving it.

Notes are ordered by instant rather than by clock reading, so notes
recorded with different time-zone offsets still sort correctly.
Notes with equal instants keep the order in which they were added.

The Developer Guide does not describe the session note types, and
the design tree still lists the timestamp source as an open
decision.

Let's describe SessionNote and SessionHistory in the Developer
Guide, and record the timestamp decision as settled: the system
date-time with its offset, ordered by instant.

Session histories need a home in the model, but the student roster
does not own session-note data, and keeping a history inside Student
would change Student equality every time a note is added.

Let's add StudentSessionHistories, which maps each StudentId to that
student's SessionHistory. It adds notes, returns an empty history for
students without notes, and removes a history while reporting how
many notes it held.

Keeping the map in its own class, as UniquePersonList does for
persons, lets AddressBook delegate to it instead of growing another
set of rules.

AddressBook holds the roster but has no session notes, so notes
cannot be stored, copied, or compared with the rest of the data.

Let's keep a StudentSessionHistories in AddressBook and expose each
student's history through ReadOnlyAddressBook. A note for a student
who is not in the roster is rejected, so every history belongs to an
existing student. resetData, equals, and hashCode now include the
histories, so copies of the address book keep their notes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add session note operations to Model
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands need a way to add, read, and remove session notes, and the
roster still reports zero notes for every student.

Let's add addSessionNote, getSessionHistory, and
removeSessionHistory to Model, and have getStudentRoster supply each
student's real note count.

ModelManager timestamps new notes with an injected Clock, truncated
to whole seconds, so that callers only pass text and tests can use a
fixed time. The existing constructors keep using the system clock.

The Developer Guide and ADR 0003 still say that roster note counts
are always zero, and the architecture notes do not name the
session-note API.

Let's describe how the model stores and exposes session histories,
note that ADR 0003's zero-count limitation is resolved, and list the
Model session-note methods as that context's entry point.

Session notes exist only in memory, so they are lost when TutorTrack
closes.

Let's add JsonAdaptedSessionNote to convert a session note to and
from JSON, with the timestamp stored as an ISO-8601 date-time and
offset. The timestamp is always written with seconds, which
OffsetDateTime#toString leaves out when they are zero, so saved files
read consistently.

Loading rejects a missing field, invalid note text, or a timestamp
without an offset, so a malformed note cannot silently become valid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Persist session notes with each student
commitResults.messageBody:
The data file stores students but not their session notes, so notes
added in one session would be lost after a restart.

Let's save each student's notes in a sessionNotes list inside that
student's JSON record, and add them back to the address book when
loading. Keeping notes inside each student's record makes the file
easy to read and edit by hand, while the model still keeps
histories separate from Student.

A missing sessionNotes field loads as an empty history, so existing
data files keep working. An empty or invalid note is a load error,
the same as an invalid student field.

The Developer Guide does not describe how session notes are stored
in the data file.

Let's document the sessionNotes JSON layout, why notes are nested in
each student's record, the timestamp format, and how missing or
malformed notes are handled when loading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add note command for session notes
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors can see each student's note count, but have no way to record
what happened in a lesson.

Let's add `note INDEX nt/NOTE`, which adds a timestamped session note
to the student at INDEX in the roster and reports the student's name.
The index is resolved against the same sorted roster that `list`
shows, and the note is stored by the student's ID.

Only nt/ is recognized, so text such as "sub/" stays part of the
note. A missing or invalid index is reported as an invalid command
format, as `delete` does. NoteCommand#toString leaves out the note
text, which may contain private lesson details.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the note workflow end to end
commitResults.messageBody:
Unit tests cover the note parser, command, model, and storage
separately, but not whether a typed note survives a restart.

Let's add an integration test that runs `add` and `note` through
LogicManager with real JSON storage, reloads the saved file, and
checks the notes, their order, timestamps, and roster counts. It
also checks that rejected `note` commands leave the data file
unchanged.

The User Guide does not mention `note`, still says roster note
counts are always zero, and does not explain how notes appear in the
data file. The Developer Guide has no design notes or manual tests
for the command.

Let's describe `note` in the User Guide with its format, rules,
examples, and errors, add it to the command summary, and explain the
sessionNotes format for users who edit the data file. In the
Developer Guide, describe how the command parses input, resolves the
index, and saves the note, and add manual-testing steps.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore data when saving a command fails
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager saves the address book after a command changes the
model, but keeps the change when saving fails. The user is told the
command failed, yet the change stays in memory and is written to the
file by the next successful save. The API contract requires a failed
save to leave the model unchanged.

Let's copy the address book before running each command and restore
the copy if saving fails, then report the same error as before.

Restoring in LogicManager covers every command, including add, note,
and delete, without each command having to undo its own changes. The
storage-failure test in LogicManagerTest now expects the model to be
unchanged, matching the contract.

The guides do not say what happens to the data when saving fails.

Let's describe the copy-and-restore step in the Developer Guide,
including the alternative of per-command undo and the remaining risk
of a partly written file. Tell users in the User Guide that a
command is cancelled when its changes cannot be saved, and record
the decision in the design tree.
